summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the confidential data drops and building a general, adaptable agent product that detects launch risks, contradictions and supplier gaps, and acts on them (emails, calls, routines) with human approval.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found that the Collector's Edition and game cards miss Sunday despite an 'all ok' plan. Built and pushed branch `jonas/today-flow` with a poller, paper check, source anchoring, routines with a When/Then/Always diagram, a verifier fix (game cards 34,800 → 6,800), a calm Today UI with email review before sending, and a two-step voice approval. Parallel builders for automation inside Today and a visual restyle were still running when the transcript ended.

repo: The portal API has only three endpoints (GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path}, /archive.zip) and no webhooks or notifications. Changes must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256, because files are replaced under the same name.

Confidential portal data lives in the gitignored `data/` folder, and `.env` is gitignored while `.env.example` is committed. The team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md, and Entire checkpoints are pushed along with git pushes.
The Entire hook only writes a checkpoint when repo files changed, and logs 'no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint' otherwise. This is expected behaviour, not a hook failure.

Real data traps: the art book receipt WZ-261116-473 was booked at 80,000 but the delivery note says 8,000. The statue lot DN-261021-819 failed AQL but is booked unrestricted. Lid magnets are a false alarm because PackRight fits them into the box. Sleeve artwork rev B (PackRight) conflicts with rev C (Nowak). Karton Nowak's offer of 8,000 art books closes the art book gap but is valid only 24 h.

The verifier originally ignored deliveries arriving before the end of packing, which showed the game-card gap as 34,800. It now counts supplier-confirmed arrivals and shows 6,800, but only after the image recognizer has read the Hwaseong shipping advice.
The image recognizer put the part number in the `item` field with an empty `material_id`, so short shipments went unrecognised until a part-number fallback was added in the doc-line mapping.

The old routines were code-only and had no recipe, so no diagram could be drawn for them and one failed on an outdated building-block API. New routines are recipes. Legacy ones were backed up to `data/state/routines.before-legacy-cleanup-050108.json`.
New routines and agent drafts now default to 'ask' mode (they prepare actions and the user sends them). Existing routines keep their mode, and saving a new version keeps the mode.

code.finding: Each part now has `arriving` (counted inbound) and `not_counted` (with reasons) lists, and gap = needed − usable − arriving. Inbound counts only if ETA is on or before launch, it is not cancelled or at the port, no goods receipt exists, it is not overdue, and the supplier document does not say less. Unread shipping documents are conservatively not counted.
The wide view was restructured into When / Then / Always lanes that wrap, with the vertical narrow view kept for the panel and phone. Planned to merge Flow/Steps/Expanded into one editable view.
All Today-screen wording is built from card fields with nothing hardcoded.
Documents the verifier changes and what is left for Farhan: the 'runs dry' time still ignores arrivals, and `impact/__main__.py` does not print the arriving list.

workflow: Delegating independent work to subagents with clearly separated file ownership (backend automation, designer, single front-end builder, verifier fix) let several parts progress in parallel without edit conflicts.
Ask before paid API calls and before pushes. The user approved the one-cent OpenAI reading, and the branch push to `jonas/today-flow` was approved separately.
When a teammate is asleep, the user preferred fixing the issue at the root and leaving a note over waiting for them.
Verify UI changes with Playwright screenshots on mocked state, and on real data by viewing only, never clicking actions that send real email.
Tests that called a now-forbidden path directly had to be updated through a shared `conftest.py` helper rather than the check being loosened.
Office-hours questions work best as pain and product questions first, with a few specific data questions to show credibility.

friction: The portal token was empty at the start, so the 401 blocked all data work until the user supplied it.
The first Entire check seemed to show the hooks had not fired, but they had. The checkpoint was skipped because no files had changed, and 7 Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
The Teams header emoji replacement missed a multi-line header and had to be fixed by hand.
Voice conversations announced an outline but then just said 'done', with no confirmation step. This required adding a server-side two-step decision with a one-time token.
The done screen offered Undo after an email had already been sent. The server refused it, so the UI was misleading.
The old code-only routines showed no diagram, and one failed on an outdated API.
The Flow, Steps and Expanded views were redundant and the one-line wide layout read poorly.
The Standard stop time was wrongly attributed to the Hwaseong card instead of the card for clear cases at the port, which needed a tie-breaker fix.
`ruff format --check` flags two pre-existing files in `dispatch/decisions`, and lint shows warnings only.
open_items: Decide whether to open a PR from `jonas/today-flow` to `main` and close PR #5, or leave the merge to Akshat.

Finish the parallel builders: automation inside Today, the unified single-view routine diagram, and the restyle of Plan, Suppliers, evidence, login and Teams. Then check screenshots, run tests, commit and push to `jonas/today-flow`.
Hand-in by Sunday 12:00 still needs a README section, demo script, 3-minute video and deck.
Phone Approve for a no-cost option sends a real supplier email immediately, and a decision on whether to keep that remains.

Register sender emails in the portal Settings and decide on an inbox for the agent to send from and read replies in. Whether portal data differs between teams, and whether our actions create new portal files, is still unknown and should be asked of the Lio engineers.
Karton Nowak's 24 h art book offer and the Boise EXW/DDP reply were not yet sent from the product.
Plan view is still dense, and the Today builder only gave it new colours.

The verifier's 'runs dry' time ignores arrivals, `impact/__main__.py` does not print the arriving list, and the 350,000 card cases at the Hamburg port are shown as a real, fixable 32,000-copy Standard risk.
Delete `data/state.json` and other portal-data snapshots after the hack. The portal password was pasted in Discord and should be changed after the hack.
The old Claude docs artifact and the briefing page still show the 14:00 state, and the user hasn't decided whether to delete the doc.
Add a local portal watcher or the deployed poller with versioned storage as a long-running process.
